1.sa: मागधा मधुभिदङ्घ्रिपङ्कजे जागरूकमपि संयमीश्वरम् । बोधयन्ति वचनैर्बुधोत्तमं काव्यवर्णनविधौ कृतादरैः ॥ १ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Oh the great saint!! kindly bestow prosperity on this world. Behold the beauty of this world with your lotus like eyes. The dawn has spread its radiance everywhere. The chanting of the Vedas is getting reverberated from all directions. Behold the dawn of such beauty. Thus addressing the great saint, the panegyrists woke him up.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मागधाः मधुभिद्-अङ्घ्रि-पङ्कजे जागरूकम् अपि संयमीश्वरम् बोधयन्ति वचनैः बुधोत्तमम् काव्य-वर्णन-विधौ कृत-आदरैः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मागधाः काव्यवर्णनविधौ कृतादरैः वचनैः मधुभिदङ्घ्रिपङ्कजे जागरूकम् अपि बुधोत्तमम् संयमीश्वरम् बोधयन्ति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The panegyrists awaken the great ascetic and foremost of the wise with carefully crafted poetic words, though he is already ever-vigilant at the lotus feet of Lord Vishnu.

2.sa: मङ्गलानि कुरु पद्मसोदरेः संयमीन्द्र जगदाहृगञ्चलैः । पश्य दृश्यविभवं दिनागमं दिक्षुदिक्षु मुखरीकृतागमम् ॥ २ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When the doors of the house filled with darkness got opened by the chanting of ruks of the Vedas by Brichaspathyacharya in the heaven, the virtuous woman (the east) who was held up there was delighted. Explanation: The woman (the east) who was held up in the house filled with darkness was unaware where she was. When she heard the chanting of the Vedas by Brihaspathyacharya in the heaven, she was delighted by learning that she was safe in Devendra's heaven.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मङ्गलानि कुरु पद्मसोदरैः संयमीन्द्र जगदाहृग्-अञ्चलैः पश्य दृश्यविभवम् दिनागमम् दिक्षु दिक्षु मुखरीकृतागमम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: हे संयमीन्द्र ! पद्मसोदरैः जगदाहृगञ्चलैः मङ्गलानि कुरु , दिक्षु दिक्षु मुखरीकृतागमम् दृश्यविभवम् दिनागमम् पश्य ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet addresses the great ascetic, asking him to shower auspiciousness through his lotus-like, benevolent sidelong glances, and invites him to behold the dawn's arrival, which is rich in visible splendor and filled with the recitation of sacred scriptures in all directions.

3.sa: पाकशासनपुरे गुरूदितेर्हन्त वेदवचनैरपाकृते । अन्धकारदुरपह्नवगेहे शक्रदिङ्मुखमिदं प्रसीदति ॥ ३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When that woman (The east) learnt that her sweetheart (Master) would come to meet her, she started constructing a canopy of pure white silk cloth (Sunlight) before his arrival. Explanation: When the sunlight spread in the east, it appeared as though the heroine (The east) was preparing to welcome him by getting a canopy of white silk cloth ready.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पाकशासनपुरे गुरु-उदितेः हन्त वेद-वचनैः अपाकृते अन्धकार-दुरपह्नव-गेहे शक्र-दिक्-मुखम् इदम् प्रसीदति
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: हन्त अन्धकार-दुरपह्नव-गेहे पाकशासनपुरे गुरु-उदितेः वेद-वचनैः अपाकृते इदम् शक्र-दिक्-मुखम् प्रसीदति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: As deep darkness is dispelled in Indra's realm by the Vedic words proclaimed by the preceptor (Guru / Brihaspati), the face of the eastern direction brightens with joy and clarity.

4.sa: शातमन्यवदिशा निजेश्वरे भानुमालिनि समागमोन्मुखे । पूर्वमेव वितनोति पाण्डिमक्षौमनिर्मलवितानमम्बरे ॥ ४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The pitch darkness in the night appears like a large herd of elephants. The dawn (the lion) destroys (rips open) the darkness (the heads of elephants). The red rays of the rising sun appearing in the east then look like the pearls of stars soaked in the blood oozing out from the heads of those elephants. Explanation: There is a belief that pearls exist in the frontal globe on the upper part of the forehead of an elephant. The poet with this in mind has described that the red sunlight in the east along with the stars looked like those pearls soaked in the blood oozing out from the heads of those elephants.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: शातमन्यवदिशा निजेश्वरे भानुमालिनि समागमोन्मुखे पूर्वम् एव वितनोति पाण्डिम-क्षौम-निर्मल-वितानम् अम्बरे
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: निजेश्वरे भानुमालिनि समागमोन्मुखे [सति], शातमन्यवदिशा अम्बरे पूर्वम् एव पाण्डिम-क्षौम-निर्मल-वितानम् वितनोति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: As her lord, the sun, is about to arrive, the eastern quarter spreads out beforehand a pure canopy of white silk across the sky (in the form of the early morning twilight).

5.sa: अन्धकारभरवारणव्रजे काल्यकेसरिविदीर्णमस्तके । शोणितौघ इव शक्रदिङ्मुखे शोणिमा लसति तारमौक्तिकैः ॥ ५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: During the war between Lord SriRama and Ravana, Indrajit the son of Ravana bound everybody with Nagapashastra. Even Sri Rama pretended as though he was bound by that Astra. Then Garuda came there and released all of them by destroying Nagapashastra. With this incident in mind, the poet has described that the darkness (Nagapashastra) which had covered (Had an intention to defeat) the sky (Sri Rama) got itself destroyed by the dawn (Garuda).
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अन्धकारभरवारणव्रजे काल्यकेसरिविदीर्णमस्तके शोणितौघः इव शक्रदिङ्मुखे शोणिमा लसति तारमौक्तिकैः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: काल्यकेसरिविदीर्णमस्तके अन्धकारभरवारणव्रजे (सति) तारमौक्तिकैः शोणितौघः इव शक्रदिङ्मुखे शोणिमा लसति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: As the lion of dawn tears open the head of the elephant of dense darkness, the reddish morning glow in the eastern sky, accompanied by bright pearl-like stars, shines like a stream of blood spilling pearls from the cleft forehead of an elephant.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: People collect honey from beehives by driving away the bees with the blaze of fire. It is interestingly explained here that the dawn is driving away the darkness (the bees) from the sky (the beehive) with the shade of glowing redness that has spread in the east (blaze of fire).
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: व्योम-राम-परिभावि-शार्वर-व्याज-पत्रगमय-अस्त्र-सन्ततेः भञ्जनाय पुरतः अरुणानुजः प्रादुः अस्ति उदय-राग-कैतवात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: व्योमरामपरिभाविशार्वरव्याजपत्रगमयास्त्रसन्ततेः भञ्जनाय अरुणानुजः उदयरागकैतवात् पुरतः प्रादुः अस्ति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Under the guise of the crimson morning glow, Garuḍa (Aruṇa's younger brother) manifested in the east to destroy the serpent-like weapon (nāgāstra) masquerading as the nocturnal darkness that enveloped the sky.

7.sa: व्योमदम्भमधुगोलसंचरद्धातसंघसरघा निराकृतिम् । आतनोति समयः पुरा दिशा शोणिमाभिशिखया विदीप्तया ॥ ७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The ocean is also known as Rathnakara. In the past, the sage Agasthya had consumed the entire quantity of water in the ocean. Then those shining rubies which were in the ocean had become clearly visible. Now when the sky (Agasthya) destroyed (drank) the darkness (the ocean) the redness of the dawn shone in the sky like those rubies.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: व्योम-दम्भ-मधुगोल-सञ्चरत्-ध्वान्त-सङ्घ-सरघा-निराकृतिम् आतनोति समयः पुरा दिशा शोणिमाभिशिखया विदीप्तया
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: समयः पुरा दिशा विदीप्तया शोणिमाभिशिखया व्योम-दम्भ-मधुगोल-सञ्चरत्-ध्वान्त-सङ्घ-सरघा-निराकृतिम् आतनोति
commentaries.gemini_summary: As dawn breaks in the eastern direction, time, radiant with blazing crimson rays, dispels the thick masses of darkness that move like a swarm of bees across the sky envisioned as a beehive.

8.sa: व्योमनामभृति कुम्भसंभवे वारिधिं पिबति शार्वराभिधम् । औषसारुणिमदम्भतः शनैः पद्मरागनिकरो विजृम्भत् ॥ ८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The blue sky becomes blackish as a result of pitch darkness. When the cloth (sky) was made (became) blackish by dying it (being covered) with more and more blue colour (darkness) its golden coloured border (tawniness of the dawn in the east) glittered like a splendid golden streak.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: व्योम-नाम-भृति कुम्भ-संभवे वारिधिम् पिबति शार्वर-अभिधम् औषस-आरुणिम-दम्भतः शनैः पद्मराग-निकरः विजृम्भत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: व्योम-नाम-भृति कुम्भ-संभवे शार्वर-अभिधम् वारिधिम् पिबति (सति) औषस-आरुणिम-दम्भतः पद्मराग-निकरः शनैः विजृम्भत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: As the sky, personified as the sage Agastya, drank up the vast ocean of the night, a heap of rubies from the ocean bed gradually shone forth under the guise of the dawn's reddish glow.

9.sa: अम्बरस्य तिमिरालिनीलिकानीलितस्य हरिदिङ्मुखाञ्चले । काल्यरक्तिमनिभेन काञ्चनीरेखिकातिरुचिरा विराजते ॥ ९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The great pugilist, the dawn intending to kill his rival, the darkness throws the dust of tawniness at him and then shows his iron fists which are reddish like the sun-disc to him. Explanation: The wrestlers or Pugilists intending to over power each other throw red dust at each other and then fight showing their fists to each other. Here the powerful dawn which is capable of killing its rival, the darkness, throws the dust of tawniness at it and then lifts its iron fists (the sun disc) to hit it.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अम्बरस्य तिमिरालि-नीलिका-नीलितस्य हरिद्-दिक्-मुख-अञ्चले काल्य-रक्तिम-निभेन काञ्चनी-रेखिका अतिरुचिरा विराजते
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तिमिरालिनीलिकानीलितस्य अम्बरस्य हरिद्दिक्मुखाञ्चले काल्यरक्तिमनिभेन अतिरुचिरा काञ्चनीरेखिका विराजते ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: On the border of the eastern horizon of the sky, which is darkened by the deep blackness of night, an exquisitely beautiful golden streak shines forth in the guise of dawn's reddish glow.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The bridegroom (the dawn) intending to enter into the wedlock with the bride (the east) tied the Mangalasutra (redness with the sun disc shining at its centre) around her neck. Explanation: In this stanza the poet has compared the dawn to a bridegroom, the east to the bride, the act of the dawn in making the east visible with its light to its intention to marry and the golden red along with sun-disc to Mangalasutra.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: काल्य-मल्ल-वरः एषः शार्वर-द्वेषि-मल्ल्यम् अभिहन्तुम् उद्यतः क्षिप्त-रक्तिम-रजाः विदर्शयति अर्क-बिम्ब-निभ-मुष्टिम् अग्रतः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: शार्वर-द्वेषि-मल्ल्यम् अभिहन्तुम् उद्यतः क्षिप्त-रक्तिम-रजाः एषः काल्य-मल्ल-वरः अग्रतः अर्क-बिम्ब-निभ-मुष्टिम् विदर्शयति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Portrayed as a champion wrestler ready to vanquish his adversary, the darkness of night, the morning dawn scatters red dust (the dawn glow) and thrusts forward his fist resembling the solar orb.

11.sa: उद्रिविक्षुहृदयो निशात्ययः प्राग्दिशं तदुपकण्ठमादधे । काल्यरागमयमादिभूषणं भानुबिम्बमणिरञ्चितान्तरम् ॥ ११ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When that beautiful girl (the east) saw her consort (the sun) with Chayadevi, her rival wife at dawn, she seething with anger kicked him with her foot smeared with the essence of lac. As a result of that kick, the sun, master of the lotus attained redness. Explanation: When a woman sees her husband with her rival wife, she kicks him with her foot adorning with the redness of the essence of lac. Likewise it appeared that the sun looked red at dawn when he was kicked by the east with her foot (the redness at dawn) which seemed to have adorned with redness of the essence of lac.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: उद्रिविक्षुहृदयः निशात्ययः प्राग्दिशम् तत्-उपकण्ठम् आदधे काल्य-राग-मयम् आदि-भूषणम् भानु-बिम्ब-मणि-रञ्जित-अन्तरम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: उद्रिविक्षुहृदयः निशात्ययः प्राग्दिशम् तदुपकण्ठम् भानुबिम्बमणिरञ्जितान्तरम् काल्यरागमयम् आदिभूषणम् आदधे ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: As night departed, it adorned the eastern quarter by placing around her neck the prime reddish glow of dawn, beautified at its centre by the jewel of the sun's rising disc.

12.sa: हन्त शक्रहरिता दिनागमे यावकारुणपदाभिताडनात् । छायया सह समागमासहात्पाटलोजनि पयोजनिश्रिता ॥ १२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The day at dawn takes a dip in the sea and wears the red Akshata (the sacred sectarian circlet) in the form of the sun disc on its forehead (the east). Explanation: The Brahmins after taking bath and completing their morning rituals wear red Akshatha (Sectarian circlet) on their foreheads. Likewise redness of the sun-disc appeared like the sectarian circlet worn by the day on its forehead (the east) after taking bath in the sea.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: हन्त शक्रहरिता दिनागमे यावक-अरुण-पद-अभिताडनात् छायया सह समागम-असहात् पाटला अजनि पयोजनिश्रिता
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: हन्त दिनागमे छायया सह समागम-असहात् शक्रहरिता यावक-अरुण-पद-अभिताडनात् पाटला (सती) पयोजनिश्रिता अजनि ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: At dawn, unable to tolerate the Sun's association with his other wife Chhāyā (shadow), the eastern quarter personified as an enraged beloved became flushed red—as if striking with feet dyed in red lac—and turned toward the blooming lotuses.

13.sa: प्रातरम्बुनि निमज्ज नीरधेरुत्थितो हरिदिशा निजालिके । अर्कमण्डलमिषेण वासरः शोणिमाक्षतललाम संदधे ॥ १३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The danseuse Divasalakshmi (the elegance of the day) after moving aside the curtain of darkness has entered the stage (the sky) creating the sound of her anklets (chirping of the birds).
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: प्रातः अम्बुनि निमज्ज नीरधेः उत्थितः हरिदिशा निज-अलिके अर्क-मण्डल-मिषेण वासरः शोणिम-अक्षत-ललाम संदधे
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: प्रातः नीरधेः अम्बुनि निमज्ज उत्थितः वासरः हरिदिशा निजालिके अर्कमण्डलमिषेण शोणिमाक्षतललाम संदधे।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having bathed in the ocean waters in the morning and risen in the east, the Day bore an auspicious red tilaka mark on its forehead in the guise of the rising sun's orb.

14.sa: अन्धकारयवनीमपाकृतामारचय्य दिवसेन्दिरा नटी । व्योमरङ्गमभजत्प्रभाञ्चितं कुर्वती खगरवेण शिञ्जितम् ॥ १४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: It appeared as if those chirping birds had entered the sky before the sun-rise itself as panegyrists of the sun who had his mind longing to conquer the group of those kings (darkness).
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अन्धकार-यवनीम् अपाकृताम् आरचय्य दिवस-इन्दिरा नटी व्योम-रङ्गम् अभजत् प्रभा-अञ्चितम् कुर्वती खग-रवेण शिञ्जितम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: दिवसेन्दिरा नटी अन्धकार-यवनीम् अपाकृताम् आरचय्य खग-रवेण शिञ्जितम् कुर्वती प्रभा-अञ्चितम् व्योम-रङ्गम् अभजत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Metaphorically portraying dawn, the goddess of daylight, like an actress, stepped onto the brightly lit stage of the sky after drawing aside the curtain of darkness, accompanied by the melodious tinkling sound of chirping birds.

15.sa: अन्धकाररिपुभूमिभृद्दृणं जेतुमुत्कमनसो विभावसोः । वन्दिनो नु बिरुदालिवाचकाः प्रागविशन्ति मुखरा विहङ्गमाः ॥ १५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When dawn set in at the end of the night, the moon who steals the hearts of those girls bereft of their sweethearts (who perturbs their minds) ran away. Then Padmini (heaps of lotus) fearlessly blossomed her lotus like eyes (Started blossoming). Explanation: The Moon disappeared just like the thieves run away, the moment the dawn set in. Padmini (the lotus) the friend of those girls who were bereft of their sweethearts was in grief as she too was separated from the sun in the night. Her grief melted away the moment dawn set in and a wide grin manifested on her face (it blossomed).
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अन्धकार-रिपु-भूमिभृत्-दृणम् जेतुम् उत्क-मनसः विभावसोः वन्दिनः नु बिरुद-आलि-वाचकाः प्राक् अविशन्ति मुखराः विहङ्गमाः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अन्धकार-रिपु-भूमिभृत्-दृणम् जेतुम् उत्कमनसः विभावसोः बिरुदालिवाचकाः वन्दिनः नु मुखराः विहङ्गमाः प्राक् अविशन्ति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: As the sun prepares eagerly to conquer the enemy king—darkness—the chirping birds appear beforehand at dawn, appearing like royal bards who arrive ahead to proclaim the king's titles and praises.

16.sa: विप्रयुक्तसखिहृन्मलिम्लुचे विद्रुते सति विधौ निशात्यये । पद्मिनी विगतसाध्वसा शनैः फुल्लमावहति पद्मलोचनम् ॥ १६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The ruddy geese which can't see anything in the dark get separated in the night and unite again, the moment the sun rises. Though they are known as chakravaka Mithuna, they form a conjugal attachment which creates a problem. Therefore the sun assigned the lotus with the task of finding a solution to this problem. The lotus which started thinking about a solution for this problem closed its eyes and remained thus throughout the night. Then it decided that when the sun rises, the problem would automatically get solved. When it saw those birds united after the sun rose, its face blossomed with a smile. This is really astonishing.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: विप्रयुक्तसखिहृन्मलिम्लुचे विद्रुते सति विधौ निशात्यये पद्मिनी विगतसाध्वसा शनैः फुल्लम् आवहति पद्मलोचनम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: निशात्यये विप्रयुक्तसखिहृन्मलिम्लुचे विधौ विद्रुते सति विगतसाध्वसा पद्मिनी शनैः फुल्लम् पद्मलोचनम् आवहति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: At the end of night, when the moon—the tormentor that robs the hearts of separated lovers—vanishes, the lotus plant is relieved of fear and slowly opens its blossoming lotus-eye.

17.sa: चक्रवाकमिथुनार्धरूपिणीं पूरयेति विहिता समस्यकाम् । मीलिताब्जनयना शुचिस्मिता पूरयत्यहह तां पयोजिनी ॥ १७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Oh Sri Raghavendra, the great saint! the moon was capriciously moving about when you, the king of the brahmins were sleeping in the night. Now when you have woken up from your sleep, the moon who has become just Dvijaraja (Master of the stars) has disappeared frightened of you. Explanation: Oh the great saint! the name Dvijaraja always suits you aptly for you are the real king of the brahmins. But when you were sleeping in contemplation in the night, the moon was whimsically moving about everywhere conjecturing that he was the only Dvijaraja (King of Stars). But now when you, the real Dvijaraja are awake, the moon, just the king of stars has disappeared apprehending that he may face your wrath.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: चक्रवाकमिथुनार्धरूपिणीम् पूरय इति विहिताम् समस्यकाम् मीलिताब्जनयना शुचिस्मिता पूरयति अहह ताम् पयोजिनी
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मीलिताब्जनयना शुचिस्मिता पयोजिनी 'चक्रवाकमिथुनार्धरूपिणीम् पूरय' इति विहिताम् ताम् समस्यकाम् अहह पूरयति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: With closed lotus eyes and a bright white smile, the lotus pond marvelously solves and fulfills the poetic puzzle (samasyā) set before it to complete the lonely half of a cakravāka pair.

18.sa: निद्रिते त्वयि पुरा द्विजाधिपे स्वैरमेव चरति स्म चन्द्रमाः । याति बोधमधुना द्विजाधिभूर्नाममात्रधृदुपैति साध्वसात् ॥ १८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The whole world was plagued by the pitch darkness which was like the smoke of separation of the ruddy geese. Now at dawn being delighted by the destruction of that darkness, it is relieved with cool breeze serving as its sigh of relief. Explanation: The pair of ruddy geese naturally get separated in the night. The smoke that emanates from the fire of their separation forms the pitch-darkness in the night. That smoke causes grief to Bhoodevi (the earth) by asphyxiating her. But when the sun rises at dawn, the earth sighs with relief as that darkness disappears.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: निद्रिते त्वयि पुरा द्विजाधिपे स्वैरम् एव चरति स्म चन्द्रमाः याति बोधम् अधुना द्विजाधिभूः नाम-मात्र-धृत् उपैति साध्वसात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पुरा द्विजाधिपे त्वयि निद्रिते चन्द्रमाः स्वैरम् एव चरति स्म अधुना द्विजाधिभूः बोधम् याति नाम-मात्र-धृत् साध्वसात् उपैति
commentaries.gemini_summary: In the past, while you—the supreme lord of the twice-born—slept, the moon roamed about at will; but now that the sovereign of the twice-born is awakening, it is reduced to merely bearing a name and retreats in fear.

19.sa: चक्रवाकविरहाग्निधूम्यया शार्वरेण जगती निपीडिता । तन्निवृत्तिसुखिताधुना ततो मन्दमुच्छ्वसति मारुतच्छलात् ॥ १९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra rose up from his bed made of tiger's skin as though he was woken up by the sprinkle of water of such sweetness of words by panegyrists.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: चक्रवाक-विरह-अग्नि-धूम्यया शार्वरेण जगती निपीडिता तत्-निवृत्ति-सुखिता अधुना ततः मन्दम् उच्छ्वसति मारुत-च्छलात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: शार्वरेण चक्रवाक-विरह-अग्नि-धूम्यया निपीडिता जगती तत्-निवृत्ति-सुखिता अधुना ततः मारुत-च्छलात् मन्दम् उच्छ्वसति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having been oppressed at night by the dark smoke from the fire of the separation of Chakravaka pairs, the earth is now relieved at dawn by its cessation, and gently breathes out a sigh of relief under the guise of the morning breeze.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Vishwa, Thaijasa, Prajna and Thureeya, the four forms of the Lord are the guiding forces respectively of the four stages namely Jagrath (wakefulness), Swapna (dreaming), Sushupthi (profound sleep) and Moksha (salvation). The form of Vishwa has nineteen faces and it always exists in the right eye. The Lord as Vishwa had an intention to listen to the discourses on nineteen sacred works comprising Dwadasha sthuti and eighteen puranas, simultaneously from Sri Raghavendra. Therefore it appeared as though the Lord Vishwa settling in the right eye of Sri Raghavendra gifted his nineteen faces to the great saint so that he could peruse all those nineteen literary works simultaneously.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: एवमादि-मागध-उक्ति-माधुरी-वारि-पूर-कृत-सेचनात् इव बोधम् एत्य यतिराट् समुत्थितः द्वीपि-चर्म-मय-तल्प-तल्लजात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यतिराट् एवमादि-मागध-उक्ति-माधुरी-वारि-पूर-कृत-सेचनात् इव बोधम् एत्य द्वीपि-चर्म-मय-तल्प-तल्लजात् समुत्थितः
commentaries.gemini_summary: As if awakened by being sprinkled with the sweet flood of words sung by the bards, the king of ascetics (Sri Raghavendra) woke up and arose from his splendid bed of leopard skin.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra, the great saint after waking up in the morning, first paid his obeisance to Lord Sri Hari. Then he profoundly paid his respects to the devathas and the gurus, superior to him in rank and accepted their blessings. Afterwards he accepted the profound respects paid by those inferior to him in rank and blessed them. He also accepted the gifts offered by his disciples.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: द्वादश-स्तुति-पुराण-संततीः श्रोतुम् आनन-समूहम् एकदा स्वम् दश-अधिक-नव-आननः अदिशत् विश्वमूर्तिः इव चक्षुरागताः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: दशाधिकनवाननः विश्वमूर्तिः इव एकदा द्वादशस्तुतिपुराणसंततीः श्रोतुम् चक्षुरागताः स्वम् आननसमूहम् अदिशत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: To hear the recitations of the Dvadasa Stotra and the lineages of Puranas all at once, he directed his assemblage of attentiveness/faces like the cosmic form (Vishvamurti) with nineteen faces appearing before the eyes.

22.sa: आनतो भवदनन्तमग्रतः संयमीन्दुरवलोक्य सञ्जनात् । आदरेण सुजनैः समर्पिताः श्रेयसे सततमाशिषोग्रहीत् ॥ २२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Then Sri Raghavendra went to Tulsi garden and prostrated before Sri Lakshmidevi indwelling in the Tulsi. Then he also prostrated in profound devotion before Sri Pranadevaru who has surrendered himself at the lotus feet of Sri Lakshmidevi and on whom Lord Sri Lakshminarayana, the consort of Sri Lakshmidevi has bestowed his special blessings.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: आनतः अभवत् अनन्तम् अग्रतः संयमीन्दुः अवलोक्य सञ्जनात् आदरेण सुजनैः समर्पिताः श्रेयसे सततम् आशिषः अग्रहीत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: संयमीन्दुः अग्रतः अनन्तम् अवलोक्य सञ्जनात् आनतः अभवत्, सुजनैः आदरेण श्रेयसे समर्पिताः आशिषः सततम् अग्रहीत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Beholding Lord Ananta present before him, the moon among ascetics (Sri Raghavendra) bowed down in reverence, and he warmly received the blessings respectfully offered by virtuous devotees for his auspicious well-being.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Then Sri Raghavendra went to the river Cauvery reputedly known as the Ganges of the south for his morning bath sitting in a sedan and chanting the hymn of Gajendramoksha in Bhagavatha.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: सः प्रणम्य तुलसी-वन-स्थिताम् इन्दिराम् तदनु तत्-पद-आश्रितम् वायुनन्दनम् अवन्दत आदरात् इन्दिरा-ईश-करुणा-एक-मन्दिरम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सः तुलसीवनस्थिताम् इन्दिराम् प्रणम्य तदनु आदरात् तत्पदाश्रितम् इन्दिरेषकरुणैकमन्दिरम् वायुनन्दनम् अवन्दत ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having offered his prostrations to Goddess Lakshmi residing in the sacred Tulasi grove, he then reverently bowed to Hanuman (Vayunandana), who has taken refuge at the Lord's feet and is the sole abode of Lord Vishnu's grace.

24.sa: सोधिरुह्य शिबिकां गजेन्द्रमुत्तयुक्तिसंस्तुतिकृतादरः शनैः । स्नातुमभ्युपगतस्तरङ्गिणीं दक्षिणापथनिलिम्पनिम्नगात् ॥ २४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The flowers of trees grown on the banks of the Cauvery attained divinity when they fell into the river. The flowers grown at other places also attained that divinity since they also belonged to the same species as that of those flowers which had attained divinity as a result of their contact with the sacred water of the Cauvery.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: सः अधिरुह्य शिबिकाम् गजेन्द्रमुक्तयुक्तिसंस्तुतिकृतादरः शनैः स्नातुम् अभ्युपगतः तरङ्गिणीम् दक्षिणापथनिलिम्पनिम्नगाम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सः शिबिकाम् अधिरुह्य गजेन्द्रमुक्तयुक्तिसंस्तुतिकृतादरः शनैः स्नातुम् दक्षिणापथनिलिम्पनिम्नगाम् तरङ्गिणीम् अभ्युपगतः।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Ascending his palanquin while graciously accepting fitting words of eulogy and praise, he proceeded slowly toward the Kaveri river, the Ganga of the South, to take his holy bath.

25.sa: तीरभूरुहसुमानि तज्जले संनिपत्य सुमनस्त्वमाप्नुवन् । जातिमात्र इति तद्गताभवद्व्याक्रियातदितरेष्वपि स्फुटम् ॥ २५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: While Samudraraja (the Ocean) was getting united in wedlock with that beautiful Cauvery adorned with coral like tides, the champak flowers grown on those trees on the river banks were looking like the rows of lamps illuminated for the occasion. Explanation: The tides of the Cauvery shine like coral at the place of confluence of the river and the sea, because of the presence of corals there. Then Samudraraja (the sea) gets united with the beautiful Cauvery who is decorated with vermillion and such other auspicious things.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: तीरभूरुहसुमानि तत्-जले संनिपत्य सुमनस्त्वम् आप्नुवन् जाति-मात्रः इति तत्-गता अभवत् व्याक्रिया तत्-इतरेषु अपि स्फुटम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तीरभूरुहसुमानि तज्जले संनिपत्य सुमनस्त्वम् आप्नुवन् । 'जातिमात्रः' इति तद्गता व्याक्रिया तदितरेषु अपि स्फुटम् अभवत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The flowers from the riverbank trees, upon falling into the sacred waters, attained true divinity and auspiciousness (sumanastva). Thus, the distinction that they were 'sumanas' merely by birth/species was clearly demonstrated and extended to all others who entered those holy waters.

26.sa: यां प्रवाललहरीं मनोहरामुद्वहन्त्यधिवसन्तम्बुधौ । तीरचम्पकसुमोत्करा लसन्त्युत्सवाय कृतदीपिका इव ॥ २६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: One need not get surprised as to how the Cauvery gets thrived by Vayu who actually dries up water and other things, the reason being that shining in infinite forms, she always enjoys the privilege of serving the Lord Sri Ranganatha with his blessings. Explanation: The Cauvery is known by a Vedic term meaning one who thrives by Vayu. The Cauvery is like Sesha, the couch of the Lord who has infinite faces, because she flows in infinite forms i.e., in different directions and always enjoys the privilege of serving the Lord Sri Ranganatha. Therefore, it is not surprising that though Vayu dries up water he serves as food of Sesha resulting in his thriving. Hence Vayu also serves Cauvery in her thriving.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: याम् प्रवाल-लहरीम् मनोहराम् उद्वहन्तीम् अधिवसन्तम् अम्बुधौ तीर-चम्पक-सुम-उत्कराः लसन्ति उत्सवाय कृत-दीपिकाः इव
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अम्बुधौ अधिवसन्तम् मनोहराम् प्रवाल-लहरीम् उद्वहन्तीं याम् तीर-चम्पक-सुम-उत्कराः उत्सवाय कृत-दीपिकाः इव लसन्ति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The clusters of champaka blossoms lining the banks of the river (Kaveri) as she bears delightful ripples of tender sprouts toward the ocean/Lord shine brilliantly, appearing like rows of festive lamps illuminated for a grand celebration.

27.sa: शोषकेण मरुता कथं नु या वर्धिता च कथमित्यविस्मयः । सा यदुल्लसदनन्तरूपिणी याति रङ्गपतिशेषतां सदा ॥ २७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The Cauvery along with her brings the sweet nectar of the heaps of lotus which have grown in Sahyaparvatha. If the water of the Cauvery was not mixed with nectar, then how could the bee (Lord Sri Ranganatha) have diverted there?
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: शोषकेण मरुता कथम् नु या वर्धिता च कथम् इति अविस्मयः सा यत् उल्लसत्-अनन्त-रूपिणी याति रङ्गपति-शेषताम् सदा
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: या शोषकेण मरुता कथम् नु वर्धिता च इति कथम् अविस्मयः यत् सा उल्लसद्-अनन्त-रूपिणी सदा रङ्गपति-शेषतां याति
commentaries.gemini_summary: There is no surprise as to how this river (Kaveri), though fostered by the drying wind (or Agastya/Vayu), prospers; for, assuming the resplendent form of the infinite serpent (Ananta), she perpetually serves as the bed of Lord Ranganatha.

28.sa: सह्यभूधरसरस्सरोजिनीसारसश्रितमरन्दसंततिम् । या बिभर्ति परथा रमेत किं तत्र रङ्गपतिभृङ्गतल्लजः ॥ २8 ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: After alighting from the sedan at the river where the atmosphere was very pleasant, Sri Raghavendra attended to nature's call, washed his hands and legs with mrittika (clay) and cleaned his teeth.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: सह्यभूधर-सरस्-सरोजिनी-सारस-श्रित-मरन्द-सन्ततिम् या बिभर्ति परथा रमेत किम् तत्र रङ्गपति-भृङ्ग-तल्लजः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: या सह्यभूधर-सरस्-सरोजिनी-सारस-श्रित-मरन्द-सन्ततिम् बिभर्ति, परथा रङ्गपति-भृङ्ग-तल्लजः तत्र किम् रमेत ?
commentaries.gemini_summary: This verse extols the river (Kaveri) which carries an abundant flow of sweet floral nectar from the lotuses of the Sahya mountain; otherwise, how could the magnificent bee, Lord Ranganatha, take such delight in residing there?

29.sa: तत्तटोपवनसीम्नि वाहनात्सोवरुह्य यमिधुर्यचन्द्रमाः । क्षालयन् करपदं समृज्जलैर्दन्तपङ्क्तिपरिशोधनं व्यधात् ॥ २९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: After achamana, Sri Raghavendra plunged into the river where he chanted the hymns three times each in profound devotion.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: तद्-तट-उपवन-सीम्नि वाहनात् सः अवरुह्य यमि-धुर्य-चन्द्रमाः क्षालयन् कर-पदम् समृज्-जलैः दन्त-पङ्क्ति-परिशोधनम् व्यधात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यमिधुर्यचन्द्रमाः सः तत्तटोपवनसीम्नि वाहनात् अवरुह्य समृज्जलैः करपदं क्षालयन् दन्तपङ्क्तिपरिशोधनं व्यधात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Dismounting from his vehicle on the edge of the riverbank grove, the great ascetic moon (Sri Raghavendra) washed his hands and feet with water and earth and cleansed his teeth.

30.sa: कल्पिताचमनमत्र सादरं स्नानकर्म कुरुते स्म शास्त्रतः । अष्टषड्द्विपदक्षैरहरेर्मानितैर्मनुवरैस्त्रिधा क्रमात् ॥ ३० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra consecrated the water chanting the sookta prescribed to be chanted during the bath and then sprinkled that water on his head. Then he smeared mrittika all over his body and again plunged into the water chanting the hymn.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: कल्पित-आचमनम् अत्र सादरम् स्नान-कर्म कुरुते स्म शास्त्रतः । अष्ट-षट्-द्वि-पद-अक्षैः हरेः मानितैः मनु-वरैः त्रिधा क्रमात् ॥
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अत्र कल्पिताचमनम् [सः] शास्त्रतः हरेः मानितैः अष्ट-षट्-द्वि-पद-अक्षैः मनु-वरैः क्रमात् त्रिधा सादरम् स्नान-कर्म कुरुते स्म ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having performed the ceremonial sipping of water (ācamana), he reverently carried out his ritual ablutions according to scriptural injunctions, chanting in three stages the revered sacred mantras of Lord Hari.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Then lifting his head above water and chanting Om, Sri Raghavendra performed ablution to Lord Sri Hari residing in his heart, chanting Om. He then took the sacred Vishnupadodaka and offered Tarpana to devathas with consecrated water.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: जप्य-सूक्त-जप-शुद्ध-वारिणा प्रोक्षयन् यतिवरः शिरः निजम् स्नातवान् विहित-मृत्-विलेपनः अनुच्छ्वसन् निरघमर्षणम् जपन्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यतिवरः जप्य-सूक्त-जप-शुद्ध-वारिणा निजं शिरः प्रोक्षयन् विहित-मृत्-विलेपनः अनुच्छ्वसन् निरघमर्षणं जपन् स्नातवान्।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Sprinkling his head with water sanctified through the chanting of sacred hymns and applying holy earth (mṛttikā), the great ascetic performed his ritual bath while holding his breath and reciting the sin-cleansing Aghamarṣaṇa hymn.

32.sa: उच्चरन्प्रणवमुत्थितोसिचत् स्वात्मगं पुरुषसूक्ततो हरिम् । विष्णुपदसलिलं पिबन् सुरास्तर्पितानकृत मन्त्रवारिभिः ॥ ३२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Then Sri Raghavendra, the great saint, enclothed himself with kaupeena and two Kashaya vastras and wore twelve urdhvapundras and five mudras with Gopichandana.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: उच्चरन् प्रणवम् उत्थितः असिचत् स्वात्मगम् पुरुषसूक्ततः हरिम् । विष्णुपदसलिलम् पिबन् सुरान् तर्पितान् अकृत मन्त्रवारिभिः ॥
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: उत्थितः प्रणवम् उच्चरन् पुरुषसूक्ततः स्वात्मगम् हरिम् असिचत्, विष्णुपदसलिलम् पिबन् मन्त्रवारिभिः सुरान् तर्पितान् अकृत ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Rising and chanting the Pranava, he bathed Lord Hari residing within his own self with the Purusha Sukta. Then, drinking the holy water of Vishnu's feet, he propitiated the gods with mantra-sanctified water.

33.sa: सालमलकमवस्तलोहिते वाससी तदनु संयमीश्वरः । ऊर्ध्वपुण्ड्रमतनिष्ट गोपिकाचन्दनेन सहपञ्चमुद्रिकम् ॥ ३३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra of great divine powers then offered arghya to devathas, meditated on Gayathri, the mother of the Vedas, in his heart and silently chanted the pranava mantra, the greatest among the hymns.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: सालमलकम् अवस्त लोहिते वाससी तदनु संयमीश्वरः ऊर्ध्वपुण्ड्रम् अतनिष्ट गोपिकाचन्दनेन सह-पञ्च-मुद्रिकम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तदनु संयमीश्वरः सालमलकम् लोहिते वाससी अवस्त, गोपिकाचन्दनेन सह-पञ्च-मुद्रिकम् ऊर्ध्वपुण्ड्रम् अतनिष्ट ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Thereafter, the lord of ascetics (Sri Raghavendra) donned two red/ochre garments and applied the vertical marks of Urdhvapundra along with the five sacred mudras using Gopicandana clay.

34.sa: अर्घ्यदानविधिमर्घ्यवैभवः संविधाय हृदि वेदमातरम् । सादरं तदनु तारकं ततो मन्त्ररत्नमपि मौनतोजपत् ॥ ३४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Then Sri Raghavendra went to Tapovana on the banks of the Cauvery where he worshipped Vyasamusthi which was previously worshipped by Sri Madhwacharya, the first guru. Afterwards he listened to the sacred stories of Lord SriHari quoted in Bhagavatha and other Puranas, from Brahmins.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अर्घ्यदानविधिम् अर्घ्यवैभवः संविधाय हृदि वेदमातरम् सादरम् तदनु तारकम् ततः मन्त्ररत्नम् अपि मौनतः अजपत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अर्घ्यवैभवः अर्घ्यदानविधिम् संविधाय तदनु हृदि सादरम् वेदमातरम् (अजपत्) ततः तारकम् मन्त्ररत्नम् अपि मौनतः अजपत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having completed the ritual offering of Arghya, the illustrious Raghavendra devoutly meditated in his heart upon the Gayatri mantra (the Mother of the Vedas), and then silently chanted the Taraka (Pranava) along with the supreme jewel of mantras.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Then Sri Raghavendra worshipped the lotus eyed Lord SriHari with ablutions of milk and water. Then he decorated the Lord with sandal paste and flowers and then offered the just prepared Huggi (a hodge podge of rice and Bengal gram) with fresh and fragrant ghee, as oblation to the Lord in profound devotion.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: तत्-तट-उपवनम् एत्य पावनीः सः अशृणोत् द्विज-मुखात् कथाः हरेः आदि-दैशिक-समर्चित-उपल-व्यास-मूर्ति-परिपूजन-उत्सुकः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तत्-तट-उपवनम् एत्य आदि-दैशिक-समर्चित-उपल-व्यास-मूर्ति-परिपूजन-उत्सुकः सः द्विज-मुखात् हरेः पावनीः कथाः अशृणोत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having arrived at the garden on the riverbank, Raghavendra, who was eager to worship the stone icon of Sri Vyasa consecrated by the ancient Guru, listened to the purifying stories of Lord Hari narrated by a brahmin.

36.sa: अभ्यषिञ्चदथ पङ्कजेक्षणं वारिभिर्व्यकृतदुग्धधारया । संन्यवेदयदयं मनोहरं मौद्गमन्नमुरुधाधिकं नवम् ॥ ३६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Then Sri Raghavendra offered his respects with profound devotion to the Brindavan of his paramaguru Sri Vijayeendra Theertha and left on his foot wearing gem studded padukas for his Mutt surrounded by many saintly scholars.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अभ्यषिञ्चत् अथ पङ्कजेक्षणम् वारिभिः व्यकृत-दुग्धधारया संन्यवेदयत् अयम् मनोहरम् मौद्गम् अन्नम् उरुधा अधिकम् नवम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अथ अयम् पङ्कजेक्षणम् वारिभिः व्यकृत-दुग्धधारया अभ्यषिञ्चत्, मनोहरम् नवम् अधिकम् मौद्गम् अन्नम् उरुधा संन्यवेदयत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Then, he performed the sacred bath (abhiṣeka) of the lotus-eyed Lord with holy waters and streams of milk, and offered an abundant quantity of delicious, freshly prepared mudga-rice (moong-dal preparation) as naivedya.

37.sa: संप्रणम्य विजयीन्द्रयोगिनं तापसोपमबुधव्रजावृतः । सोधिरुह्य मणिरम्यपादुके दैशिको मठमथ प्रतस्थिवान् ॥ ३७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: While Sri Raghavendra was returning to his Mutt, the sounds of musical instruments like conch, kettle, drum, mridanga, trumpet, double drum, horn and chakra played by his servants were reverberating from all directions.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: संप्रणम्य विजयीन्द्रयोगिनम् तापसोपमबुधव्रजावृतः सः अधिरुह्य मणिरम्यपादुके दैशिकः मठम् अथ प्रतस्थिवान्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अथ तापसोपमबुधव्रजावृतः सः दैशिकः विजयीन्द्रयोगिनम् संप्रणम्य मणिरम्यपादुके अधिरुह्य मठम् प्रतस्थिवान् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Surrounded by a group of ascetic-like scholars, the preceptor bowed reverently to Vijayindra Tirtha, put on his gem-studded sandals, and departed for his monastery.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra who appeared like the embodiment (manifestation) of Devaloka's Kalpavruksha sanctifying the earth with his each step while returning entered his Mutt after paying his obeisance to Kumbheshwara, the consort of Parvathi on his way.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: शङ्ख-दुन्दुभि-मृदङ्ग-काहली-मड्डु-डिण्डिम-सुशृङ्ग-झर्झरैः चक्र-वाद्य-निनदैः च तत्-जनाः पूरयन्ति पुरतः अस्य दिक्-मुखम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तत्-जनाः अस्य पुरतः शङ्ख-दुन्दुभि-मृदङ्ग-काहली-मड्डु-डिण्डिम-सुशृङ्ग-झर्झरैः चक्र-वाद्य-निनदैः च दिक्-मुखम् पूरयन्ति।
commentaries.gemini_summary: His followers filled the quarters of the sky in front of him with the resonant sounds of various musical instruments, such as conches, dundubhi drums, mridangas, flutes/horns, dindimas, jharjharas, and cymbals.

39.sa: पावयन्नथ महीं पदेपदे पार्वतींशमभिवन्द्य पङ्क्तौ । प्राविशत्ससुर विष्टपागमो मूर्तिमानिव मठं तथागमः ॥ ३९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The great scholar used to deliver discourses specially on Brahmasutra Bhashya in the assembly of scholars. He also used to refute other systems of Indian philosophy.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पावयन् अथ महीम् पदे पदे पार्वती-ईशम् अभिवन्द्य पङ्क्तौ प्राविशत् ससुर-विष्टप-आगमः मूर्तिमान् इव मठम् तथा आगमः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अथ पदे पदे महीं पावयन् पङ्क्तौ पार्वती-ईशम् अभिवन्द्य ससुर-विष्टप-आगमः मूर्तिमान् आगमः इव तथा मठं प्राविशत्
commentaries.gemini_summary: Purifying the earth at every step and bowing to Lord Shiva along the row, he entered the monastery like the very scriptures (Agamas) personified, accompanied by divine presence.

40.sa: शान्तिवाचनपुरस्सरं वरं भाष्यमेव स विशिष्य संसदि । व्याकरोति विदुषां निराकरोत्यन्यदर्शनकुयुक्तिसंहतिम् ॥ ४० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When Sri Raghavendra said that the soothras have propounded that Sri Narayana whom the learned men worshipped, had unlimited qualities, free from defects, intelligible and cognisible which has been found as the essence of sootras by Sri Anandatheertha, three scholars put forth their points of view before the saint, in an agitated manner.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: शान्तिवाचन-पुरस्सरम् वरम् भाष्यम् एव सः विशिष्य संसदि व्याकरोति विदुषाम् निराकरोति अन्य-दर्शन-कुयुक्ति-संहतिम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सः संसदि विदुषां शान्तिवाचनपुरस्सरं वरं भाष्यम् एव विशिष्य व्याकरोति अन्यदर्शनकुयुक्तिसंहतिं निराकरोति
commentaries.gemini_summary: Preceded by the chanting of peace prayers, he specifically expounded the supreme commentary (Bhashya) before the assembly of scholars, thoroughly refuting the host of fallacious arguments from opposing philosophical schools.

41.sa: ब्रह्म सद्गुणमदोषमीक्षितं गम्यमाहुरिव लक्षणैः क्रमात् । सूत्रभाष्य इति तेन भाषिते तत्र कश्चन सुधीरचोदयत् ॥ ४१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: We are not convinced of your explanation. Who is Narayana? 'I' is the only thing known by experience. It is very difficult to accept any other thing without evidence. Perception or inference does not admit any other thing as real. According to Shruthis, 'Parabrahma' as described in the Vedas is not different from the 'Jeeva' or 'I'. When it is established that both 'Brahma' and 'Jeeva' are same, where is the need for the shastras teaching about Brahma? Then if we talk about difference, high and low ranks are false. Only the experience of 'I' by the 'Jeeva' is true. Even the 'I' disappears as and when it grows further and the experience of intelligence which alone is true remains. If so, where is the question of 'Narayana', the 'Parabrahma' having attributes? It is impossible to worship such a thing. As Maya from which stems the attitude to consider that two things are different, vanishes, one attains salvation. Therefore the belief that one could attain salvation with the aid of other things is an illusion. It is enough if we perform Karma to attain Swargaloka. Therefore this 'Brahma Meemamsa' is meaningless.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: ब्रह्म सद्गुणम् अदोषम् ईक्षितम् गम्यम् आहुः इव लक्षणैः क्रमात् सूत्रभाष्ये इति तेन भाषिते तत्र कश्चन सुधीः अचोदयत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तेन सूत्रभाष्ये 'ब्रह्म क्रमात् लक्षणैः सद्गुणम् अदोषम् ईक्षितम् गम्यम् आहुः' इति भाषिते (सति), तत्र कश्चन सुधीः अचोदयत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: When he explained that the Sutra-Bhashya describes Brahman through various characteristics sequentially as possessing all auspicious attributes, flawless, perceptible, and attainable, a certain intelligent scholar in the assembly raised an objection.

42.sa: नित्यवाग विषयस्य सर्वथाऽरम्भणं न विषयस्य युज्यते । नामधेयमिह यज्जडं मृषा जातमर्थरहितं स्वचिन्तनन् ॥ ४२ ॥

commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: नित्य-वाक्-विषयस्य सर्वथा आरम्भणम् न विषयस्य युज्यते नामधेयम् इह यत् जडम् मृषा जातम् अर्थ-रहितम् स्व-चिन्तनम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: नित्यवाग्विषयस्य विषयस्य आरम्भणं सर्वथा न युज्यते । इह यत् जडं नामधेयं जातम्, (तत्) अर्थरहितं मृषा स्वचिन्तनम् (अस्ति) ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Arguing from an Advaitic standpoint invoking the Upanishadic concept of 'vācārambhaṇam', the speaker contends that inert, objective phenomena cannot truly be designated by eternal sacred speech, as all such material names and objects are false, insubstantial, and mere products of conceptual thought.

43.sa: नात्मतत्त्वमपि तत्र नापरश्चेष्टितादिबहुलिङ्गसिद्धितः । जीवभिन्नपरमोप्यमानको न स्वयं च यदहंधिया यतः ॥ ४३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: We are not convinced of your explanation. Who is Narayana? 'I' is the only thing known by experience. It is very difficult to accept any other thing without evidence. Perception or inference does not admit any other thing as real. commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: न आत्मतत्त्वम् अपि तत्र न अपरः चेष्टितादि-बहु-लिङ्ग-सिद्धितः । जीव-भिन्न-परमः अपि अमानकः न स्वयम् च यत् अहम्-धिया यतः ॥
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तत्र चेष्टितादि-बहु-लिङ्ग-सिद्धितः आत्मतत्त्वम् अपि न [असिद्धम्], अपरः न [अस्ति]। जीव-भिन्न-परमः अपि अमानकः, यत् च यतः [सः] अहंधिया स्वयम् न [सिद्धः] ॥
commentaries.gemini_summary: The opponent argues that while the individual soul is readily established through various signs like bodily actions and efforts, a separate Supreme Being distinct from the soul lacks valid proof and is not experienced in one's direct self-awareness ('I'-cognition).

44.sa: किंच किं फलममुष्य वेदने कर्मणैव भवति स्वरादिकम् । नापि मुक्तिरधुनैव तद्विदां दृश्यते न यदसावपि क्वचित् ॥ ४४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: We are not convinced of your explanation. Who is Narayana? 'I' is the only thing known by experience. It is very difficult to accept any other thing without evidence. Perception or inference does not admit any other thing as real. Therefore this 'Brahma Meemamsa' is meaningless.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: किंच किम् फलम् अमुष्य वेदने कर्मणा एव भवति स्वः-आदिकम् । न अपि मुक्तिः अधुना एव तत्-विदाम् दृश्यते न यत् असौ अपि क्वचित् ॥
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: किंच अमुष्य वेदने किं फलम् ? कर्मणा एव स्वरादिकं भवति । तद्विदां मुक्तिः अपि न (भवति), यत् अधुना एव असौ अपि क्वचित् न दृश्यते ॥
commentaries.gemini_summary: The opponent questions the purpose of knowing Brahman, arguing that heaven and other results are attained purely through ritual action (karma), while liberation is not visibly attained even now anywhere by those possessing such knowledge.

45.sa: अत्र कश्चिदमभ्यचोदयच्छुद्धमस्य विषयं स्वमानसम् । शुद्धवेदनफलं वदेन्न चेद्धन्धभङ्ग इति किं ततो वद ॥ ४५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: We are not convinced of your explanation. Who is Narayana? 'I' is the only thing known by experience. It is very difficult to accept any other thing without evidence. Perception or inference does not admit any other thing as real. According to Shruthis, 'Parabrahma' as described in the Vedas is not different from the 'Jeeva' or 'I'. When it is established that both 'Brahma' and 'Jeeva' are same, where is the need for the shastras teaching about Brahma? Then if we talk about difference, high and low ranks are false. Only the experience of 'I' by the 'Jeeva' is true. Even the 'I' disappears as and when it grows further and the experience of intelligence which alone is true remains. If so, where is the question of 'Narayana', the 'Parabrahma' having attributes? It is impossible to worship such a thing. As Maya from which stems the attitude to consider that two things are different, vanishes, one attains salvation. Therefore the belief that one could attain salvation with the aid of other things is an illusion. It is enough if we perform Karma to attain Swargaloka. Therefore this 'Brahma Meemamsa' is meaningless.

46.sa: इत्युदीरितगिरातिरोषितस्यद्वचः प्रतिवचोन्य आददे । यत्तु शुद्धमुदितं न मानसं तन्नयुक्तमिति हन्त चिन्त्यते ॥ ४६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: We are not convinced of your explanation. Who is Narayana? 'I' is the only thing known by experience. It is very difficult to accept any other thing without evidence. Perception or inference does not admit any other thing as real. According to Shruthis, 'Parabrahma' as described in the Vedas is not different from the 'Jeeva' or 'I'. When it is established that both 'Brahma' and 'Jeeva' are same, where is the need for the shastras teaching about Brahma? Then if we talk about difference, high and low ranks are false. Only the experience of 'I' by the 'Jeeva' is true. Even the 'I' disappears as and when it grows further and the experience of intelligence which alone is true remains. If so, where is the question of 'Narayana', the 'Parabrahma' having attributes? It is impossible to worship such a thing. As Maya from which stems the attitude to consider that two things are different, vanishes, one attains salvation. Therefore the belief that one could attain salvation with the aid of other things is an illusion. It is enough if we perform Karma to attain Swargaloka. Therefore this 'Brahma Meemamsa' is meaningless.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: इति उदीरित-गिरा अतिरोषित-स्यद्वचः प्रतिवचः अन्यः आददे यत् तु शुद्धम् उदितम् न मानसम् तत् न युक्तम् इति हन्त चिन्त्यते
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: इति उदीरित-गिरा अतिरोषित-स्यद्वचः अन्यः प्रतिवचः आददे—हन्त यत् तु शुद्धम् न मानसम् उदितम् तत् न युक्तम् इति चिन्त्यते।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Incensed by the preceding speech, another opponent swiftly offered a rebuttal, asserting that it is flawed to regard the ultimate reality as purely non-conceptual and beyond mental perception.

47.sa: यन्न भाति जडजीवभेदनं कर्तृतादिविरहोऽद्वितीयता । एकतापि तदसारमात्मनोऽभिन्नमैतदिति चेदसंशयः ॥ ४७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The Swamiji found a great opportunity to preach the real Tattva to his pious disciples when those scholars put forth their queries before him. Then he began replying the scholars.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: यत् न भाति जडजीवभेदनम् कर्तृतादिविरहः अद्वितीयता एकता अपि तत् असारम् आत्मनः अभिन्नम् एतत् इति चेत् असंशयः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यत् जडजीवभेदनम् कर्तृतादिविरहः अद्वितीयता एकता अपि न भाति तत् असारम् । एतत् आत्मनः अभिन्नम् इति चेत् असंशयः (आत्मा अपि असारः स्यात्) ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: This verse presents a dialectical critique stating that if distinctions (such as between matter and the soul), the absence of agency, non-duality, and oneness are not manifest, they are devoid of substance; if they are held to be identical with the Self, the Self itself inevitably becomes unreal/unsubstantial.

48.sa: अन्यदेतदिति नापि युक्तिमत्संमृषेति हि विकलप्नक्षमम् । तत्स्वरूपमिति चेन्न भासते तत्र नैव तव युज्यते श्रमः ॥ ४८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The Swamiji found a great opportunity to preach the real Tattva to his pious disciples when those scholars put forth their queries before him. Then he began replying the scholars.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अन्यत् एतत् इति न अपि युक्तिमत् संमृषा इति हि विकल्पना-अक्षमम् तत्-स्वरूपम् इति चेत् न भासते तत्र न एव तव युज्यते श्रमः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: एतत् अन्यत् इति अपि न युक्तिमत्, संमृषा इति हि विकल्पना-अक्षमम् । तत्स्वरूपम् इति चेत् न भासते, तत्र तव श्रमः न एव युज्यते ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Refuting the opponent's philosophical position, the verse states that asserting something as entirely distinct is unreasonable and cannot withstand the dilemma of truth versus falsity; moreover, if it is claimed to be its essential nature yet does not manifest, the opponent's intellectual effort is utterly futile.

49.sa: अत्र तद्भ्रमनिरासनोत्सुकः सस्मितं सदयमब्रवीद्गुरुः । अस्ति किंचिद्हमर्थतः परं विष्णुनाम गुणपूर्णम तम् ॥ ४९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Your objections have no validity, because it does not mean that only the things experienced or seen by man in his daily life are true. There are many true things which are beyond his ken. It is only for realising this truth, man is gifted with intelligence which is superior to that of animals. One would be experiencing in his daily life an intuition about the existence of this invisible truth. Things which are invisible to defective eyes could be seen with healthy eyes. Many things which are invisible to the naked eyes could be seen with the help of accessories. A poet or an artist would be immersed in emotions which are beyond the imagination of an ordinary man. Everybody cannot realise that many surprising things in the world are controlled and guided by a power beyond their imagination. It is beyond the abilities of our faculties of understanding to understand such things. It is the nature of the man to approach the source in which he has confidence to understand the things beyond his imagination. The Vedas are such a source. The Intellectuals can realise that the Vedas are Sadagamas. This source is not the creation of modern times. It must have been in existence since eternity. It must be as eternal as eternity itself. At the same time it must have been uncreated. To know its real meaning, a proper reasoning is essential. Then only, one can understand clearly the real meaning of the contradictions in these Shastras. One would not have been yearning to understand such contradictions, if they were as clear as the visible things. That must emerge from cohesive churning of thought. These Sadagamas mainly deal with the subject related to Brahman. Some thoughts propounding the identity of 'Brahma' and the individual soul referred to as 'I' could also be found here and there. But such thoughts should be interpreted by proper reasoning. If the meaning is accepted as it is, then the need of studying the Vedic lore does not arise. If it is accepted that the 'Jeeva' who undergoes misery everyday is 'Brahma' himself, then all the activities of this world would come to stand still. Rather than getting convinced by such vague interpretations, it would be most acceptable and honest if the thoughts that treat the identity are discussed thoroughly taking into consideration the context of the beginning and the end of the passage, the rules of grammar adopted in arriving at their meaning, helpful arguments, etc. and analysing whether such thoughts could be interpreted differently leading to a conclusion which is not detrimental to the supremacy of 'Brahma'. This is the main task of the Brahma Sootras. These Sootras would not have advocated the necessity of the study of the nature of 'Brahma' by the 'Sadhaka', had the identity been the ultimate meaning of the Vedas. Therefore there is no need to declare that 'Brahma Meemamsa Shastra' is most essential for the aspirant of 'Adhyatma Tattva'. Sri Anandatheertha has convincingly proved that this is the real meaning of the Sootras. Only Lord Sri Narayana, the abode of infinite qualities and who is absolutely flawless is 'Parabrahma'. To be always meditating on him is the secret of life. To realise him is the fulfilment of life. Life is full of love, not hollow but tested and found pure on the touchstone of joys and sorrows. The God is the source of such love which results in bliss. This is the essence of Shastras. This is the principle of life".
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अत्र तत्-भ्रम-निरासन-उत्सुकः स-स्मितम् स-दयम् अब्रवीत् गुरुः अस्ति किञ्चित् अहम्-अर्थतः परम् विष्णु-नाम गुण-पूर्णम् अद्भुतम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अत्र तत्-भ्रम-निरासन-उत्सुकः गुरुः सस्मितं सदयम् अब्रवीत् - अहम्-अर्थतः परं गुण-पूर्णम् अद्भुतं विष्णु-नाम किञ्चित् अस्ति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Eager to dispel their misconceptions, the Guru smiled and kindly explained that distinct from and superior to the individual self ('I'), there exists a wonderful supreme reality named Vishnu, who is complete with all auspicious attributes.

50.sa: यद्विचारविषये निगद्यते ब्रह्मनाम परजीवभेदकम् । मुक्तिरेव फलमस्य वेदनात्प्रक्रमोस्य विषयादिमांस्ततः ॥ ५० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra thus concluded his argument. All the disciples of the Swamiji were overwhelmed with joy. The scholars who raised the queries prostrated before the swamiji with a sense of shame about their ignorance.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: यत्-विचार-विषये निगद्यते ब्रह्म-नाम पर-जीव-भेदकम् मुक्तिः एव फलम् अस्य वेदनात् प्रक्रमः अस्य विषय-आदिमान् ततः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यत्-विचार-विषये पर-जीव-भेदकम् ब्रह्म-नाम निगद्यते अस्य वेदनात् फलम् मुक्तिः एव ततः अस्य प्रक्रमः विषय-आदिमान्
commentaries.gemini_summary: Since the Supreme Brahman, who is distinct from the individual souls, is declared as the subject of this inquiry and liberation is the fruit of knowing Him, the commencement of this philosophical treatise is well-endowed with the necessary subject matter and purpose.

51.sa: एवमादिपरमात्मचिन्तनैरास्त संयमिवरोतिहर्षितः । तत्र सानुभवलिप्सया दिवो मध्यसीमानि रविर्व्यलम्बत ॥ ५१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra, the great saint remained in a state of bliss by discussing such things with regard to the greatness of the Lord. The sun too who had an intention to listen to those scholarly discussions slowed down his pace of movement in the sky. Explanation: Usually the sun appears to move very slowly in the noon. It is exaggerated here that as the sun too had an intention to know more about the greatness of Parabrahma, he slowed down his pace when he saw Sri Raghavendra in discussion with other scholars.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: एवम्-आदि-परमात्म-चिन्तनैः आस्त संयमि-वरः अति-हर्षितः तत्र सानुभव-लिप्सया दिवः मध्य-सीमानि रविः व्यलम्बत
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: संयमिवरः एवमादि-परमात्म-चिन्तनैः अतिहर्षितः आस्त । तत्र सानुभव-लिप्सया रविः दिवः मध्यसीमानि व्यलम्बत ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Immensely delighted by meditating upon and discussing the Supreme Lord in such ways, the eminent ascetic remained absorbed, while the sun lingered at midday in the sky as if eager to listen to that divine discourse.

52.sa: अस्ते ध्वान्ते समस्ते प्रतिभटसरणीं गत्वरे प्रादुरासी- च्छायारूपं तदेतच्छरणमुपगतं पादमूलं जनानाम् । हन्तामन्दप्रतापे रपि मम किरणैः शक्यते तन्न भेत्तुं धिङ्मामित्याकुलोर्कः प्रतपति कलयन्न्योममध्ये विलम्बम् ॥ ५२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: As the dawn set in and the sun rose, the darkness started getting annihilated. The sun started destroying the darkness, his enemy wherever it was found, with his light. Then that darkness transformed itself into shadow and took refuge under the soles of the people. "It is really shameful for me, for I have failed to destroy this darkness completely even with my blazing rays!" thus abusing himself, the sun who was disgusted started moving slowly in the sky tormenting the people with his blazing heat.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अस्ते ध्वान्ते समस्ते प्रतिभट-सरणीम् गत्वरे प्रादुरासीत् छाया-रूपम् तत् एतत् शरणम् उपगतम् पाद-मूलम् जनानाम् हन्त अमन्द-प्रतापैः अपि मम किरणैः शक्यते तत् न भेत्तुम् धिक् माम् इति आकुलः अर्कः प्रतपति कलयन् व्योम-मध्ये विलम्बम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: समस्ते ध्वान्ते अस्ते प्रतिभट-सरणीम् गत्वरे (सति), छाया-रूपम् तत् एतत् जनानाम् पाद-मूलम् शरणम् उपगतम् प्रादुरासीत् । हन्त, अमन्द-प्रतापैः मम किरणैः अपि तत् भेत्तुम् न शक्यते, माम् धिक् इति आकुलः अर्कः व्योम-मध्ये विलम्बम् कलयन् प्रतपति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: When the vast darkness was banished, it took refuge as shadows beneath the feet of people; distressed that even his intensely blazing rays could not pierce it there, the sun lingered at midday in the sky, scorching fiercely in self-reproach.

53.sa: वक्राम्भोजं विधत्ते मम सुहृदमिति प्राप्तरॊषो विवस्वान् म्लानं मीनेक्षणानां नयनयुगमयं क्लपयन्न्लब्णश्रीः । तच्छायाधारिणोस्मानपि तपति मुहुस्तं समाधेहि पाही- त्यारादम्भोजिनीनां शकुलकुलमयादाकुलं पादमूलम् ॥ ५३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "The sun is agitated seeing those fish like eyes of beautiful girls reducing to nothing the splendor of their lotus like faces, which are like his friends. Therefore he is not only causing dimness in those eyes but also is tormenting us constantly with his glaring rays, because we look like those eyes. Kindly console the enraged sun and protect us" praying thus, the fishes hid under the stems of the lotus.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वक्त्राम्भोजम् विधत्ते मम सुहृदम् इति प्राप्तरोषः विवस्वान् म्लानम् मीनेक्षणानाम् नयनयुगम् अयम् क्लपयन् उल्बणश्रीः तत्-छाया-धारिणः अस्मान् अपि तपति मुहुः तम् समाधेहि पाहि इति आरात् अम्भोजिनीनाम् शकुलकुलम् अयात् आकुलम् पादमूलम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अयम् मम सुहृदं वक्त्राम्भोजं म्लानं विधत्ते इति प्राप्तरोषः उल्बणश्रीः विवस्वान् मीनेक्षणानां नयनयुगं क्लपयन् तच्छायाधारिणः अस्मान् अपि मुहुः तपति, तं समाधेहि, पाहि इति आकुलं शकुलकुलम् आरात् अम्भोजिनीनां पादमूलम् अयात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Angered that the fish-like eyes of lovely maidens diminished the beauty of their lotus-like faces (his friend), the sun tormented not only their eyes but also the fish who resembled them; thus distressed, the school of fish took refuge under the roots of the lotus plants, pleading for protection.

54.sa: माद्यन्दिनस्नानकृते महान्तं मुनीन्द्रमित्थं किल कालशंसी । आगत्य मध्यन्दिनस्नानमस्मै न्यवेदयत्प्राप्तमहत्सचेताः ॥ ५४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: As the noon approached, the timekeeper courteously appealed to Sri Raghavendra to get ready for the noon bath. Explanation: When the noon approached as described in stanzas 52 and 53, the timekeeper requested the saint to get ready for the noon bath.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: माद्यन्दिनस्नानकृते महान्तम् मुनीन्द्रम् इत्थम् किल कालशंसी आगत्य मध्यन्दिनस्नानम् अस्मै न्यवेदयत् प्राप्तम् अहः सचेताः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सचेताः कालशंसी आगत्य माद्यन्दिनस्नानकृते महान्तम् अस्मै मुनीन्द्रम् 'अहः प्राप्तम्' (इति) इत्थं किल मध्यन्दिनस्नानं न्यवेदयत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The mindful timekeeper approached the venerable sage Raghavendra and respectfully announced that the midday hour had arrived, urging him to prepare for his midday bath.

55.sa: व्याख्याय शिष्यनिवहाय चिराय सोय- माम्नायमौलिवचनानि मनोहराणि । माध्याह्निकानि विविधानि विधातुकामः कर्माणि मन्दमुदतिष्ठदुदग्रकीर्तिः ॥ ५५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Thus the greatly celebrated saint Sri Raghavendra continued his discourse on Brahma Sootra Bhashya giving heart stirring quotes from Upanishads as illustrated for his disciples till noon. Then he rose up from his seat to perform different religious rituals pertaining to noon.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: व्याख्याय शिष्यनिवहाय चिराय सः अयम् आम्नायमौलिवचनानि मनोहराणि माध्याह्निकानि विविधानि विधातुकामः कर्माणि मन्दम् उदतिष्ठत् उदग्रकीर्तिः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सः अयम् उदग्रकीर्तिः शिष्यनिवहाय मनोहराणि आम्नायमौलिवचनानि चिराय व्याख्याय विविधानि माध्याह्निकानि कर्माणि विधातुकामः मन्दम् उदतिष्ठत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having expounded the delightful words of the Upanishads at length to the assembly of his disciples, the highly renowned saint slowly arose, desiring to perform his various midday religious rites.

56.sa: निष्कुटविलसत्पुष्करवत्यां पुष्कलकीर्तिर्मस्करिधुर्यः । साधु निमज्ज्य सुधीजनमान्यो माधवमङ्गलगेहमयासीत् ॥ ५६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra, the great saint who had an unmatched fame and who was revered by those men of knowledge took bath in that splendid lake situated in the garden at the backyard of the Mutt and came to the sacred pooja hall of Sri Moolarama.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: निष्कुट-विलसत्-पुष्करवत्याम् पुष्कल-कीर्तिः मस्करि-धुर्यः साधु निमज्ज्य सुधी-जन-मान्यः माधव-मङ्गल-गेहम् अयासीत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पुष्कलकीर्तिः सुधीजनमान्यः मस्करिधुर्यः निष्कुटविलसत्पुष्करवत्याम् साधु निमज्ज्य माधवमङ्गलगेहम् अयासीत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The renowned foremost of ascetics, who was revered by wise scholars, bathed properly in the splendid garden pond and then proceeded to the auspicious shrine of Lord Madhava.

57.sa: डम्भासोढा काममम्भोरुहाख्यैरम्भःपूर्णं कुम्भमादौ समर्च्य । आत्मन्नान्तर्मातृकादीनशेषान् देवान् देवैः पीठगैः पार्श्वगैश्च ॥ ५७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra who was intolerant towards dishonesty and fraudulence first worshipped the Kalasha (Jar) filled with pure water, with flowers like lotus, which lasted for a long time. Then after invoking the presence of Matrika devathas and other devathas along with Peethabhimani devathas and Parivara devathas in that water, he offered ablution to the Saligramas and the idol of the lotus eyed Sri Moolarama with that consecrated water.

58.sa: शालिग्रामानम्बुजाक्षस्य मूर्तिं मन्त्राम्भोभिः संयमीन्द्रोभिषिच्य । नव्यैः पुष्पैरातनिष्टातिरम्यै रत्नैरर्ध्यं रामचन्द्रस्य पूजाम् ॥ ५८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Then he decorated the idol of Sri Moolarama with all the nine glittering gems and worshipped the Lord with fresh flowers and offer of Arghya and other services with profound devotion.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: शालिग्रामान् अम्बुजाक्षस्य मूर्तिम् मन्त्र-अम्भोभिः संयमीन्द्रः अभिषिच्य नव्यैः पुष्पैः आतनिष्ट अतिरम्यैः रत्नैः अर्ध्याम् रामचन्द्रस्य पूजाम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: संयमीन्द्रः मन्त्राम्भोभिः शालिग्रामान् अम्बुजाक्षस्य मूर्तिम् अभिषिच्य नव्यैः पुष्पैः अतिरम्यैः रत्नैः रामचन्द्रस्य अर्ध्याम् पूजाम् आतनिष्ट ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having bathed the Shaligrama stones and the icon of the lotus-eyed Lord with mantra-consecrated water, the king of ascetics performed the exquisite worship of Lord Ramachandra using fresh flowers and charming gemstones.

59.sa: वाजिमेधयजिना विकल्पितं शङ्खवारि शिरसा स धारयन् । राजसूययजिनापि सम्मतं विष्णुपादसलिलं पिबत्यसौ ॥ ५९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Then Sri Raghavendra sprinkled Shankodaka (Consecrated water from the conch) which was considered equal to Ashwamedhayaga on his head and also had Sri Vishnupadodaka which was considered more sacred than Rajasuyayaga. Explanation: It is customary to sprinkle Shankodaka on the head before taking theertha after worshipping Lord Sri Hari. It is believed that the sprinkling of Shankhodaka is equal to Avabrithasnana (Bath taken at the conclusion) after Ashwamedhayaga. The scholars also opine that consumption of theertha in the form of Sri Haripadodaka is more sacred than Avabrithasnana after Rajasuyayaga.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वाजिमेधयजिना विकल्पितम् शङ्खवारि शिरसा सः धारयन् राजसूययजिना अपि सम्मतम् विष्णुपादसलिलम् पिबति असौ
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: असौ सः वाजिमेधयजिना विकल्पितं शङ्खवारि शिरसा धारयन् राजसूययजिना अपि सम्मतं विष्णुपादसलिलं पिबति।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Bearing on his head the consecrated conch water, deemed comparable in merit to the Ashvamedha sacrifice, he (Raghavendra) partakes of the sacred water from Lord Vishnu's feet, which is revered as equal to the Rajasuya sacrifice.

60.sa: स्वत कवेरजापयोनघं हि किं पुनर्हरेः । पदं समाश्रितं चतुःपुमर्थदं भवेदिति ॥ ६० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The water of the river Cauvery is renowned as naturally most sacred. Then, is it necessary to declare that the Cauvery water getting into contact with the lotus feet of Lord Sri Hari at the time of ablution is capable of bestowing all the four objects of a soul!!
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: स्वतः कवेरजा-पयः अनघम् हि किम् पुनः हरेः पदम् समाश्रितम् चतुः-पुमर्थ-दम् भवेत् इति
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: कवेरजापयः स्वतः हि अनघम्, हरेः पदम् समाश्रितम् (तत्) चतुःपुमर्थदम् भवेत् इति किम् पुनः?
commentaries.gemini_summary: The water of the river Kaveri is inherently pure and sinless; it goes without saying that upon coming into contact with the lotus feet of Lord Hari, it becomes capable of granting all four goals of human life.

61.sa: पश्चात्कृत्वा हरिपादनतिं संयमीन्द्रोथ भुक्त्वा पुण्यं भैक्ष्यं तदनुरचयन् तर्कशब्दादिशास्त्रैः । विद्वद्वपूर्वाविधनगरात्प्राप्तवद्भिर्विनोदं ध्यायन्विष्णुं समयमनयत्सोयमासायमेवम् ॥ ६१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra, the emperor of the family of saints prostrated at the lotus feet of Lord Sri Hari after taking Theertha. Then he had the sacred lunch prepared for him and offered to Lord Sri Hari as oblation. Afterwards he spent his time till evening by discussing Tarka and Vyakarana with the scholars who had come there from different places, in a spirit of entertainment and enlightenment which he ultimately dedicated to Lord Sri Narayana.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पश्चात् कृत्वा हरि-पाद-नतिम् संयमि-इन्द्रः अथ भुक्त्वा पुण्यम् भैक्ष्यम् तदनु रचयन् तर्क-शब्द-आदि-शास्त्रैः विद्वद्-वर्यैः बहु-विध-नगरात् प्राप्तवद्भिः विनोदम् ध्यायन् विष्णुम् समयम् अनयत् सः अयम् आ-सायम् एवम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अथ पश्चात् सः अयम् संयमीन्द्रः हरिपादनतिं कृत्वा पुण्यं भैक्ष्यं भुक्त्वा तदनु बहुविधनगरात् प्राप्तवद्भिः विद्वद्वर्यैः तर्कशब्दादिशास्त्रैः विनोदं रचयन् विष्णुं ध्यायन् आसायम् एवं समयम् अनयत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: After bowing at the feet of Lord Hari and partaking of the sanctified alms-meal, the great ascetic Sri Raghavendra spent his time until evening immersed in the contemplation of Lord Vishnu while engaging in scholarly and intellectual discussions on logic and grammar with learned scholars who had arrived from various cities.

62.sa: श्रीमत्कश्यपवंशवार्धिशशिनः षड्दर्शनीवल्लभ श्रीलक्ष्मीनरसिंहवित्तविदुषः श्रीवेङ्कटाम्बामणौ । जातेनार्यदयासुधामयगिरा नारायणेनोदिते काव्ये चारुणि राघवेन्द्रविजये सर्गोभवन्नवमः ॥ ६२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Thus concludes the ninth canto of the epic "Sri Raghavendra Vijaya" enchanting with amrosial words composed by Narayanacharya with the blessings of his father. Narayanacharya who had his education from his father was the son of the couple Venkatamba and Lakshminarasimhacharya who was an erudite scholar in all the six Shastras and who was born and shone like a moon in the ocean of Kashyapa gothra named after that virtuous and scholarly sage Kashyapa. English translation of the ninth canto of the epic "Sri Raghavendra Vijaya" composed by Sri Narayanacharya concluded.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रीमत्-कश्यप-वंश-वार्धि-शशिनः षड्दर्शनी-वल्लभ-श्री-लक्ष्मीनरसिंह-वित्त-विदुषः श्रीवेङ्कटाम्बामणौ जातेन आर्य-दया-सुधामय-गिरा नारायणेन उदिते चारुणि राघवेन्द्रविजये काव्ये नवमः सर्गः अभवत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: श्रीमत्-कश्यप-वंश-वार्धि-शशिनः षड्दर्शनी-वल्लभ-श्री-लक्ष्मीनरसिंह-वित्त-विदुषः श्रीवेङ्कटाम्बामणौ जातेन आर्य-दया-सुधामय-गिरा नारायणेन उदिते चारुणि राघवेन्द्रविजये काव्ये नवमः सर्गः अभवत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: This colophon verse marks the conclusion of the ninth canto of the beautiful epic Raghavendra Vijaya, composed with speech enriched by the nectar-like grace of his father/preceptor by Narayanacharya, who was born of Sri Venkatamba and the erudite scholar Lakshminarasimha—the master of the six philosophical systems and the moon rising from the ocean of the Kashyapa lineage.
